h: Everything you need to run the network
Built for real-time multi-vendor fault handling
subpages.text: Products Solutions Partners About Us Contact Career Resources Speak to Us Home / products / EvoΝΕΤ EvoΝΕΤ EvoNET is a powerful network management platform that ensures full visibility, automation, and control across your infrastructure. It delivers the complete operations cycle for multi-vendor transport networks - from automatic discovery through topology, monitoring, and fault management to service provisioning - through a single web interface. Download Brochure Why EvoNET Transport networks are rarely built from a single vendor. Growth, acquisitions, and best-of-breed procurement leave most teams managing equipment from many suppliers - each with its own element manager, its own CLI, and its own idea of how faults should be reported. The operational cost is not the hardware; it is correlating what all of it is doing at once. EvoNET removes that fragmentation. It discovers equipment automatically from defined IP pools, identifies each device's type and vendor, and places it in a hierarchical tree by region, site, or your own criteria. From that single inventory it drives the full lifecycle - polling, remote configuration, backup, firmware, and service provisioning - the same way across every supported vendor, through a flexible driver model with adapters for Nokia, Infinera, Eltex, and more. Fault handling is where a multi-vendor NMS earns its place. EvoNET collects events over SNMP Traps, Syslog, and NETCONF, guards itself with built-in Storm Control, and passes everything through an intelligent Fault Management Module that correlates alarms, suppresses duplicates and flapping, and classifies by severity - then notifies the right staff by email according to rules you define. subpages.text: Products Solutions Partners About Us Contact Career Resources Speak to Us Home / products / VelOS-SP VelOS-SP VelOS-SP is a carrier-grade network operating system purpose-built for service provider networks, delivering full IP/MPLS, precision timing, and segment routing on whitebox hardware, with seamless integration into existing OSS/BSS and network management systems through open standards. It is the carrier-grade NOS that frees operators from proprietary lock-in without compromising on protocol depth or network resilience. Download Brochure Why VelOS-SP Service provider networks are not data centre networks, and they should not be served by a data centre NOS with service provider features bolted on. VelOS-SP is purpose-built from the ground up for the demands of telecom and ISP environments -- every protocol, every feature, and every operational workflow is designed for service provider networks. VelOS-SP delivers the full IP/MPLS protocol stack that carrier-grade networks demand: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), Open Shortest Path First (OSPF), Intermediate System to Intermediate System (IS-IS), Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS), and Segment Routing (SR-MPLS and SRv6). From mobile backhaul to metro aggregation to core routing, VelOS-SP provides the protocol depth and resilience that operators have relied on for decades -- now available on open whitebox hardware, with native integration into existing OSS/BSS toolchains and network management systems. Carrier-grade reliability is not optional in service provider networks -- it is the baseline. VelOS-SP delivers precision timing with IEEE 1588v2 and Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE), Operations, Administration, and Maintenance (OAM) with CFM and Y.1731, and Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD) for sub-second failover.

subpages.text: Products Solutions Partners About Us Contact Career Resources Speak to Us Home / products / VelOS-DC VelOS-DC VelOS-DC is a data centre network operating system built from the ground up on Linux -- not layered on top of it. It integrates natively with compute environments, automation frameworks, and AI/GPU cluster fabrics, delivering hyperscaler-grade networking on whitebox hardware -- with seamless integration into existing infrastructure through open standards. Download Brochure Why VelOS-DC Data centre networks are not general-purpose infrastructure -- they are the foundation on which every compute workload, every storage operation, and every AI training job depends. The network operating system that runs the fabric must be as native to the data centre environment as the servers it connects. VelOS-DC is Linux -- not a proprietary system with a Linux compatibility layer bolted on. The kernel is the source of truth for network state, and every tool a Linux engineer already knows works out of the box. Ansible playbooks configure switches the same way they configure servers. Systemd manages network services the same way it manages compute services. Shell scripts, cron jobs, and standard Linux utilities operate without translation layers or proprietary CLI abstractions. This is what Linux-native means: the network operates as a first-class member of the compute environment, not an isolated appliance managed through a separate toolchain. VelOS-DC runs on NeoX data centre switches built on industry-standard Broadcom silicon -- from Trident 3 leaf switches to Tomahawk 4 hyperscale spines. subpages.text: Products Solutions Partners About Us Contact Career Resources Speak to Us Home / solutions / Service Provider Networking Service Provider Networking Service-provider backbone, aggregation and provider edge routing are the most critical layers in a service provider network. VelOS SP delivers the full IP/MPLS protocol stack, multi-service delivery with Ethernet Virtual Private Network (EVPN), Layer 2 VPN (L2VPN), Layer 3 VPN (L3VPN), and Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) with seamless integration into existing OSS/BSS and transport infrastructure through open standards. Book a Consultation Download Brochure Carrier-Grade Aggregation and PE Routing on Open Hardware About Evollabs Evollabs Tech delivers a next-generation service provider aggregation environment designed for telecom operators, ISPs, and managed service providers building scalable metro and provider edge networks. Built on deep IP/MPLS and carrier networking expertise, our platform enables organizations to deploy, optimize, and scale multi-service aggregation infrastructure with carrier-grade reliability and operational flexibility. THE CHALLENGE The aggregation layer in service provider networks concentrates traffic from thousands of access nodes, cell sites, and enterprise connections into the metro or region core. Traditionally, this layer is built on heavy, complex and power-hungry chassis-based provider edge (PE) routers -- platforms built based on a proprietary and closed silicon hardware and sold at premium pricing. When an operator needs to add capacity, the options are limited: purchase another proprietary chassis at significant capital expenditure or upgrade to the next chassis model in the same vendor's portfolio. h: AI/GPU Cluster Fabric with VelOS DC
subpages.text: Products Solutions Partners About Us Contact Career Resources Speak to Us Home / solutions / AI Data Centre Networking AI Data Centre Networking AI training workloads demand a network fabric where every packet arrives, every time. VelOS DC delivers production-ready RDMA over Converged Ethernet version 2 (RoCEv2), Priority Flow Control (PFC), Explicit Congestion Notification (ECN), Data Center Quantized Congestion Notification (DCQCN) and Dynamic Load Balancing (DLB) -- giving GPU clusters the lossless, low-latency fabric with seamless integration into existing AI infrastructure through open standards. Book a Consultation Download Brochure Lossless Ethernet for GPU Clusters - Shipping Today on Open Hardware About Evollabs Evollabs delivers a production-ready, lossless Ethernet fabric specifically engineered to eliminate the bottlenecks of distributed AI training. By integrating RoCEv2, PFC, and DCQCN on open NeoX hardware, we provide the zero-tolerance, low-latency environment required for massive GPU clusters to synchronize gradients without stalling. Our Linux-native approach ensures that your network fabric operates with the same precision and automation as your compute nodes, maximizing GPU utilization and accelerating time-to-insight. THE CHALLENGE Distributed AI training is fundamentally a networking problem. When hundreds or thousands of GPUs collaborate on a training job, they must synchronise gradients after every iteration -- exchanging massive volumes of data across the fabric with minimal latency and zero tolerance for packet loss.
